To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CTE-WBEs exist, that they achieve the CTE-TSC lower bound, and that the user capacity of the system can be characterized in terms of the received SINR.
CTE-WBES are jointly optimum transmit sequences in continuous-time, overloaded MISO CDMA systems with AWGN channels and that the matched filter is the jointly optimum receiver.

there exists a set of jointly optimum continuous-time transmit sequences that achieve the minimum total MSE for the band-limited MISO channels and that these sequences are the continuous-time equivalents of WBE sequences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of continuous-time equivalent sequences and receivers that are optimal for overloaded CDMA systems.
the development of a general framework for the optimization of the continuous-time MISO system for the overloaded channels with additive white Gaussian noise.
the continuous-time equivalents of WBE sequences and the continuous-time equivalent total squared correlation (CE-TSC) bound, which is a generalization of the discrete-time TSC bound.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CTE-WBE sequence design and analysis is the continuous-time equivalent to the discrete-time sequence optimization and analysis.
CTE-WEB sequences are the optimal solutions to the continuous-time multiple-access channel problem with equal-power users and that they achieve the maximum user capacity of such channels.

, for a given number of users in a continuous-time, band-limited multiple-access channel, the CTE-WBE waveforms and the corresponding matched filter receivers achieve the maximum SINRs and the maximum total SINR, and that they are the only waveforms that achieve the lower bound of the total squared correlation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the discrete-time theory of Welch bound equality is extended to continuous-time, band-limited channels, where it is shown that CTE-TSC and user capacity can be achieved by CTE-WBE waveforms and matched filters.
the CTE-WBE waveforms are optimal for overloaded CDMA systems operating in band-limited continuous-time channels.
the CTE-WBE sequence optimization is a powerful tool to characterize the user capacity of the overloaded band-limited multiple-access channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTE-WB sequences are the jointly optimum transmit and receive waveforms for the continuous-time MISO channel.
the CTE-WBE waveforms can be used to design optimum waveforms in a variety of scenarios where a continuous-time model is more appropriate than a discrete-time model.
CTE-WWE sequences are the optimum transmit waveforms for overloaded band-limited multiple-access systems with AWGN.
